ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs, and authorized representatives against the United Nations Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, South African FIC targeted financial sanctions list, and South African domestic PEP lists. Enhanced due diligence is triggered for any politically exposed person, based on FIC Guidance Note 7A. Results must be retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in the Roman/Latin alphabet. Names using non-Roman scripts or languages other than English or Afrikaans must be accompanied by an approved transliteration. Names must comply with section 11 and section 12 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008, must not be offensive, misleading, or confusingly similar to an existing registered name or trade mark.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If CIPC refuses to reserve a name, the applicant or its authorized attorney may submit a written reconsideration request through the CIPC e-Services portal within 20 business days. If the refusal is sustained, the applicant may appeal to the Companies Tribunal under section 167(3) of the Companies Act within 30 business days of the notice of refusal. The appeal must be filed using the prescribed Companies Tribunal form and paid when made. Reapplication using a distinct, compliant name is also available without prejudice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is acceptable for the statutory registered office only, provided it is supplied by a licensed registered-office service provider maintaining a physical street address in South Africa and all legal documents can be validly served. A post office box alone is prohibited. For high-altitude rope access and facade contracting, the company must maintain an operational business site (storage, safety equipment, and management premises) and sufficient employees, assets, and local decision-making to demonstrate commercial substance for tax and licensing purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium-risk: approximately 30% annual probability of unannounced physical inspection. Competent authorities include the Department of Employment and Labour under OHSA for construction/rope access, CIPC compliance inspections, SARS verification visits, and FIC inspections for AML/CFT record keeping. The likelihood increases if a workplace incident or complaint is reported.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, as amended; Companies Regulations, 2011 (GN R351 of 28 April 2011); s13 (incorporation), s14 (effect of incorporation), s15 (memorandum of incorporation), s66 (board of directors), s69 (first directors), s70 (election of directors); Regulation 14 (Notice of Incorporation, CoR 14.1).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), 77 Meintjies Street, Pretoria, South Africa.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (CoR 14.1), Memorandum of Incorporation (CoR 14.2), and Director Consent forms (CoR 14.3).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up share capital prescribed under the Companies Act 71 of 2008; shares may be allotted for nil or nominal consideration; no escrow account requirement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, at the first board meeting of [Company Name] (Pty) Ltd held at its registered office on [date]: 1. The incorporation under the Companies Act 71 of 2008, per Notice of Incorporation and Memorandum of Incorporation, is ratified in full. 2. The directors' subscription for the initial issued share capital is accepted and share certificates issued as recorded in the share register. 3. The registered office is fixed at [address], South Africa. 4. The following officers are appointed until the next annual general meeting: [Director 1] as Managing Director, [Director 2] as Chief Financial Officer, and [Director 3] as Company Secretary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Pre-Registration Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search on the CIPC e-Services portal; file Form CoR 9.1 (Application for Reservation of Company Name) with a first-choice name and up to two alternative names; pay the prescribed fee online via credit/debit card or electronic funds transfer.
required_dossiers: CoR 9.1 Application for Reservation of Company Name
Certified identification documents of incorporators
Proof of payment of name reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected for undesirability or confusing similarity, file a fresh CoR 9.1 with alternative names or submit a formal objection under section 160 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting the Memorandum of Incorporation and Director Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Appointed legal counsel / external company secretary (pre-lodgement preparation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum of Incorporation using the standard CoR 14.2 template or bespoke provisions; complete incorporators' consent and directors' written consent (CoR 14.3); declare the registered office and postal address; verify the initial directors satisfy the suitability requirements under section 69.
required_dossiers: CoR 14.2 Memorandum of Incorporation (standard or custom)
CoR 14.3 Director Consent forms
Registered office and postal address particulars
Certified ID or passport copies of directors and incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Amend any defective or inconsistent Memorandum of Incorporation provisions prior to lodgement and resubmit corrected CoR 14.3 consent forms.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Lodgement of Notice of Incorporation with CIPC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online incorporation application in CIPC e-Services; attach CoR 14.1 Notice of Incorporation, the Memorandum of Incorporation, and director consent forms; declare compliance with section 13; pay the prescribed private company incorporation fee of ZAR 175 (approximately USD 10); upon successful processing obtain the CIPC Registration Certificate and unique company registration number.
required_dossiers: CoR 14.1 Notice of Incorporation
CoR 14.2 Memorandum of Incorporation
CoR 14.3 Director Consent forms
Proof of payment of incorporation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried by CIPC, respond within the prescribed period by filing a supplementary CoR form or corrected data; re-lodge the application with full compliance after curing the noted defects.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Constitution of the Board and Corporate Governance Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors and CIPC company record
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting to adopt the formal First Board Resolution, allot the initial share capital, confirm the registered office, and appoint the managing director, chief financial officer, and company secretary; execute and retain the minutes, share register, register of directors, and appointment letters; file CoR 29 with CIPC if any director particulars change after incorporation.
required_dossiers: Signed First Board Resolution and minutes
Register of Directors and Share Register
Officer appointment letters
CoR 29 (if updating director particulars with CIPC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify any governance inconsistency by passing a supplementary board resolution; file CoR 29 within the statutory 10-business-day window to correct director records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) via eFiling; Compensation Fund; Unemployment Insurance Fund (UIF); Construction Industry Development Board (CIDB)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for income tax (ITREG), employer registration (EMP101), and VAT (VAT101) on SARS eFiling within 21 days of incorporation; register as an employer with the Compensation Fund under the Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act (COIDA) and with the UIF; for public-sector tenders, apply for CIDB contractor grading in the appropriate construction works class.
required_dossiers: CIPC Certificate of Incorporation
Memorandum of Incorporation and First Board Resolution
SARS registration forms (ITREG, EMP101, VAT101)
Directors' certified identification and proof of address
COIDA employer registration form (W.As. 2)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to SARS verification or information requests with supporting corporate documents; liaise with the departmental registration desks to clear duplicate filings or outstanding queries.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Department of Employment and Labour (Occupational Health and Safety Division); Construction Industry Development Board (CIDB)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Contractor Health-and-Safety Compliance File under Section 37.2 of the Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993 and Construction Regulations, 2014; CIDB Contractor Grading Registration.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE) — Environmental Authorisation Branch
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — routine façade maintenance and glass replacement are not listed as scheduled activities under Listing Notices 1, 2, or 3 of the EIA Regulations, 2014 under NEMA (Act 107 of 1998); however, waste handling obligations under the National Environmental Management Waste Act 59 of 2008 remain applicable.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero process wastewater discharge from rope-access operations; runoff containment and spill kits required. Volatile organic compound and solvent emissions from sealants, adhesives, and cleaning agents must comply with the National Environmental Management Air Quality Act 39 of 2004 and SANS 10400 thresholds. Waste sealant containers, broken glass, and used abrasives must be classified as general or hazardous waste under the Waste Classification and Management Regulations and removed by licensed waste transporters.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the municipal fire authority covering working-at-height rescue plans and hot-work permits; structural load inspection of façade anchors, suspension lines, and rigging equipment by a competent person per SANS 50274-1 and EN 795; workplace clearance certificate evidencing compliance with the designation of a fall protection plan, mandatory risk assessment, and appointment of a construction health-and-safety officer on site.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); portal: www.sars.gov.za and SARS eFiling (secure online filing system)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A domestic (Pty) Ltd is first incorporated with the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC). Within 21 business days of incorporation or commencing business, the company must apply to SARS for income-tax registration via eFiling (form ITREG or electronic equivalent). For VAT, the company must submit a VAT 101 application (or eFiling equivalent) to the applicable SARS branch. Foreign non-resident entities must appoint an SARS-recognised representative taxpayer. Supporting documents: CIPC registration certificate and Memorandum of Incorporation, directors' identity documents or passports, shareholders' details, physical registered address in South Africa, and banking details. SARS issues an Income Tax Reference Number and, on approval, a VAT registration number (10 digits for VAT vendors) with an assigned tax period.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (resident South African company taxed on worldwide income at the 27% corporate income tax rate; distributions to non-resident shareholders attract Dividends Tax withheld at 20%)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa has no 'check-the-box' regime; corporate classification follows the Income Tax Act 58 of 1962. Relevant elections: (1) Small Business Corporation (s12E) reduced-rate status for a qualifying Pty Ltd whose shareholders are all natural persons; (2) voluntary VAT registration under s23(2) of the VAT Act where taxable turnover exceeds ZAR 50,000 but is below the ZAR 1,000,000 compulsory threshold; (3) VAT cash accounting (payments basis) election under s9B for vendors with taxable turnover under ZAR 2,500,000; (4) the OECD-aligned anti-hybrid rules (s23M) apply automatically with no remedial election; (5) for indirect taxes, grouping of connected companies under s50(3) of the VAT Act allows a single vendor registration only on SARS approval.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory registration: ZAR 1,000,000 of taxable supplies in the preceding 12 months under s23(1)(a); voluntary registration from ZAR 50,000 under s23(2); separate rule: foreign suppliers of electronic services are required to register without a threshold
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No statutory real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping mandate currently applies in South Africa. SARS supports voluntary OECD-standard 'SARS Authenticated E-Invoicing' (ASEIC) under s20(6) of the VAT Act, with phased modernisation expected. All vendors must issue SARS-compliant tax invoices under s20 of the VAT Act reflecting the words 'Tax Invoice'; VAT returns are lodged via eFiling; export zero-rating is substantiated by documentary proof of physical export retained for audit.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exported goods: zero-rated under s11(1)(a) of the VAT Act where goods are supplied to a non-resident and exported within 90 days after the date of supply, with documentary proof of export obtained within 12 months. Export services: zero-rated under s11(2)(l) where supplied to a non-resident and the services are not used or consumed in South Africa. EXCEPTION ALERT: services physically performed on, or connected to, immovable property situated in South Africa (including rope-access structural glass works) do NOT qualify for s11(2)(l) zero-rating, even if invoiced to a foreign non-resident client; such work is standard-rated at 15% VAT. Any qualifying exports must also satisfy the Exchange Control requirement that proceeds be received in foreign currency and evidenced by an Inward Remittance Certificate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD500) through the SARS Customs clear-and-pay process
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill / Road Manifest evidencing physical export
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) from an authorised foreign-exchange dealer
SARS proof-of-export documentation file retained for five years
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS conducts risk-scored audits of export refunds and may retrospectively disallow zero-rating and claw back claimed input VAT. Statute-backed consequences include: assessment of 15% VAT on the full invoiced value; additional tax under s60 of the VAT Act of up to 200% where non-disclosure or misrepresentation is not bona fide; 10%-20% understatement penalties under ss222-223 of the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011; market-rate interest; and potential criminal prosecution for tax fraud. Fraudulently obtained refunds are recoverable in full and refunds may be frozen pending audit.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Financial Surveillance Department of the South African Reserve Bank (SARB FinSurv), acting under the Currency and Exchanges Act, 1933 and Exchange Control Regulations, 1961
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Africa maintains a partially convertible currency. Current account payments by authorised dealers are generally permitted with supporting documentation. Capital account flows require either authorised dealer approval or SARB FinSurv approval for amounts exceeding delegated limits. Non-resident holding company profit remittances (dividends, branch profits, management fees) are permitted under exchange control provided the underlying capital has been duly reported and applicable South African withholding taxes (dividend tax or interest withholding) have been settled. No automatic central bank approval is required for routine dividend remittances from audited profits, but all capital repatriation must be recorded through authorised dealers for balance-of-payments statistics and may be subject to documentary verification.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exports of goods must be paid in full within 90 days of shipment (extension is possible only with valid commercial justification and prior SARB FinSurv authorisation). All export proceeds received in foreign currency must be converted into rand via an authorised dealer within 30 days of receipt, unless the exporter holds an approved Foreign Currency Account (FCA). Advance payments for goods not yet shipped must be deposited with the exporter's authorised dealer within a prescribed deadline and normally require a guarantee or confirmed order.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Standard Bank (Standard Bank of South Africa Limited)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (Current Account in ZAR) with foreign currency denomination capability
Operational Account plus Capital Import / Export escrow facilities
Operational Account with trade finance module and e-Filing exchange control integration
Operational Account and segregated Foreign Investment escrow sub-account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility for inbound capital or operational liquidity. Offshore digital EMI accounts (e.g. multi-currency wallets not regulated by SARB FinSurv) cannot serve as authorised dealers for conversion of export proceeds into ZAR and cannot hold funds in trust for a South African resident without violating the Exchange Control Regulations. Global licensed EMIs may be used only for outbound administrative payments to foreign suppliers where the underlying transaction is supported by invoices and cleared via the authorised dealer; even then the bank flagship relationship remains mandatory.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a foreign-owned South African Pty Ltd, the founding directors and 25%-plus beneficial owners are generally required to undergo a face-to-face KYC interview at the onboarding bank branch. Several Tier-1 banks permit an exception with a notarised and apostilled board resolution, certified passport copies, and a video-sanctioned interview for reputable OECD-source applicants; however, physical presence of at least one authorised signatory is still the de facto compliance default under FICA for corporate accounts exhibiting beneficial ownership complexity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-altitude rope-access facade construction is classified as construction sector activity; under FICA, construction entities may be screened for money-laundering risk through subcontractor transactions and cross-border payments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare a project-specific invoice ledger, the signed construction contract with the property owner, subcontractor supplier agreements, proof of trade references, and audited financial statements demonstrating that all payments are contractually tied to completed structural glass replacement milestones.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership concentration or an offshore parent with tax-haven holding structure may trigger enhanced due diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) share registry, an updated Register of Beneficial Ownership, a corporate organogram, notarised affidavits from each ultimate beneficial owner, and a clear statement of the funding sources for share capital, including bank reference letters and source-of-funds evidence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound foreign-currency receipts to fund working capital create concerns over proper exchange control designation and potential impurity of capital account flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the executed subscription agreement/shareholder loan agreement, the SARB FinSurv 'CSD' (Capital Structured Deal) declaration or EM/1 report, proof of conversion through the authorised dealer, and the bank's letter confirming successful recording as foreign direct investment for balance-of-payments purposes.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound share capital must be remitted by S.W.I.F.T. wire (or CHAPS) from the non-resident shareholder's bank to the authorised dealer within South Africa. The instructions must specify the company name, the account number, the payment purpose code 'CG' or 'Capital Contributions' (purpose code may vary by bank but must clearly indicate 'foreign direct investment in equity capital'), and the underlying share subscription contract. The authorised dealer must be provided a completed EM/1 form for inward foreign investment (or the relevant SARB reporting template), and the funds must be held in a designated account until conversion to ZAR at the prevailing spot rate. Hard-copy verification of the non-resident's identity, the share allotment resolution, and the South African Revenue Service (SARS) tax registration number of the Pty Ltd must be submitted within 30 days.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for incurred liabilities should be cleared via SWIFT MT103 (single customer credit transfer) for high-value structural glass procurement and via a Commercial Letter of Credit (documentary credit subject to UCP 600) where the glass system supplier requires guarantees of payment against shipping documents. All outward payments must be made by the authorised dealer in South Africa and charged to the company's ZAR account, being converted to the invoice currency. For cross-border settlement with South Africa's SACU partners, deferred payment by bulk electronic transfer through the Common Payments System may be considered, but the MT103 and LC rails remain the default under exchange-control-supervised banking.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable forward exchange contracts (FECs) with an authorised dealer covering a committed underlying import or export exposure in USD, EUR, or GBP
Currency swaps entered into solely to hedge the principal and interest exposure on an approved cross-border construction credit facility, subject to SARB FinSurv authorisation

FX options (European style) written by the authorised dealer to protect the ZAR cost of a planned major import of facade materials, provided the underlying commercial transaction is evidenced and no naked optionality exists

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after the anniversary of the date of incorporation (company registration date).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a non-compliance fee; continued failure may result in administrative deregistration by CIPC after two consecutive missed annual returns, following a final warning and statutory notice period (typically 60 to 90 days).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Register Annual Confirmation (filed together with the Annual Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Simultaneously with the Annual Return on the same anniversary-based deadline (within 30 business days after the incorporation anniversary).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incomplete annual return may be rejected with CIPC non-compliance penalties; deliberate failure to file beneficial ownership information is an offence under the Companies Act 2008.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A full compulsory independent audit is required where the company's Public Interest Score (PIS) for the financial year is 350 or higher; for a public company, state-owned company, or where a regulatory licensing sector mandates an audit. A PIS between 100 and 349 requires an independent review unless the MOI or shareholders voluntarily resolve to apply a full audit. A private company with a PIS below 100 is generally exempt from audit and independent review, subject to specific legal or regulatory obligations.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as issued by the IASB, or IFRS for SMEs for eligible small and medium enterprises, both recognized under the Companies Act 2008.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must maintain an internal Beneficial Ownership Register and include a beneficial ownership declaration in the annual CIPC return. Any shareholding transfer or change in beneficial ownership must be filed with CIPC within 5 business days of the change, in addition to the annual confirmation; where no change occurs, a nil confirmation is submitted with the Annual Return.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 - USD 600 annual fee for a registered agent/office in Johannesburg or Cape Town.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - USD 7,500 for a full statutory audit in the specialist construction and facade access sector if the PIS threshold is met; exempt companies incur USD 0.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Corporation (SBC) graduated rates apply where gross income is below ZAR 20 million, all shareholders are natural persons, and the company is not a personal service provider: 0% on first ZAR 95,000; 7% on ZAR 95,001–365,000; 21% on ZAR 365,001–550,000; 27% above ZAR 550,000. Additional deductions: s.11(d) wear-and-tear, s.12B renewable energy allowance (125%), s.12C machinery allowance (40/20/20/20), and Employment Tax Incentive for qualifying employees.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite (no statutory time limit; annual set-off of assessed losses capped at 80% of taxable income under s.20(1A))

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ITR14 (Company Income Tax Return) filed electronically via SARS eFiling; mandatory eFiling for provisional taxpayers. Provisional tax payments are recorded on IRP6 returns.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; provisional tax (IRP6) paid twice per year (at months 6 and 12 of the year of assessment) with an optional third top-up payment within 6 months after year-end.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: ITR14 must be submitted within 12 months of the financial year-end, or such later date as SARS determines in the notice containing the return; provisional payments are due on or before the last day of month 6 and the last day of month 12 of the year of assessment; the voluntary third top-up is due within 6 months after year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box A — Company Particulars / Public Officer
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered name, registration number, tax reference number, financial year-end, trade classification code, public officer identity. The public officer must be a bona fide resident individual employed by the company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder or director cannot act as public officer; the form requires a resident contact person and a local registered business address.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross receipts from rope-access facade contracts, including progress billings (Progress_ACH) and wire transfers received, before any deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Revenue earned by the South African company forms part of its gross income even where invoicing is directed to a foreign principal; convert foreign-currency receipts at the ruling exchange rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions under s.11(a): subcontractor costs, equipment hire and low-value consumables, insurance, employee costs, s.12C machinery and tool allowances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border recharge payments to a related offshore entity must satisfy the arm's-length test in s.31; otherwise deductions are disallowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Items exempt under s.10, e.g., foreign dividends (subject to the participation exemption), fair values of certain instruments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign dividend exemption requires the South African company to hold at least 10% of the payer's voting rights; documentary proof must be retained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year assessed loss brought forward and applied, limited to 80% of current-year taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the company's ownership changes in contemplation of a foreign acquisition, the loss set-off may be denied under the s.20A anti-loss-trading rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box F — Taxable Income and Tax Payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income computed after set-offs and capital gain inclusion (80% of net capital gain); tax applied at 27% (or the SBC graduated scale); rebates and credits deducted.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the SBC rate only if all shareholders are natural persons; a corporate or non-resident-owned entity is taxed at a flat 27%.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: First and second provisional payments credited against the assessed tax; any third top-up payment credited.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders cannot bear the company's provisional tax liability; underestimation of taxable income by more than ZAR 1 million or 20% triggers a 20% estimate penalty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declared dividends to shareholders, identification of resident vs non-resident beneficial owners, and DWT withheld at 20%.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Withhold 20% from dividends to non-residents unless a valid declaration and tax residency certificate are on file for treaty-exempt (e.g., 10% participation) relief; failure to withhold makes the company liable for the tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: Administrative Non-Compliance Penalty (ANP) of up to ZAR 16,000 per month for large businesses and ZAR 4,000 per month for small companies, plus a daily penalty of up to ZAR 250 per day. Late payment: 10% late-payment penalty plus interest at the prescribed rate (Repo + 7 percentage points). Underestimation of provisional tax: 20% of the shortfall. Criminal default may attract a fine of up to ZAR 50,000 and/or imprisonment up to 2 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% (Dividend Withholding Tax under s.64EA–64H of the Income Tax Act; payable by the company as withholding agent on dividends declared to non-resident beneficial owners; exempt where the beneficial owner is a foreign company holding at least 10% of the shares, or in specified jurisdictions-companies circumstances)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a reduced DWT rate (typically 5%–15% under South African DTAs), the non-resident shareholder must submit, before payment of the dividend, a signed SARS declaration and undertaking form (DTR.01 for dividends; DTR.02 for interest; DTR.03 for royalties) together with a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the home-country tax authority, to the South African company as withholding agent; the company retains the documents for audit and applies the treaty rate at source. If documents are incomplete, DWT is deducted at 20% and the excess can be recovered via a refund application through SARS.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rate: 15% for royalties and 15% for interest paid to non-residents. Treaty rates commonly range from 0% to 12% for both royalties and interest depending on the DTA and beneficial-ownership conditions (e.g., reduced rates for bank interest and approved industrial royalties).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Section 31 ITA regulates all cross-border related-party transactions on an arm's-length basis. Mandatory contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation (TP policy, Local File, Master File) is required where the aggregate value of cross-border related-party transactions exceeds ZAR 100 million in a year of assessment; below the threshold, SARS may still demand documentation in an audit, and any related-party transaction must be supported by written pricing evidence (TNMM is widely used).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Africa does not maintain a separate UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations filing regime, but SARS applies OECD BEPS substance-over-form principles, the general anti-avoidance rule (s.103), and anti-treaty-shopping rules; a company claiming treaty benefits or foreign tax credits must demonstrate real hiring decisions, local employees, physical premises, bank accounts, and business purpose, failing which SARS can reconstruct transactions, deny deductions, or treat the entity as a conduit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Omitting cash or wire-transfer proceeds from high-altitude rope-access contracts, overstating subcontractor costs, destroying daily site records, or submitting false IRP6 estimates to defer provisional tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Understatement penalty of 100%–200% of the shortfall for intentional and intentional-after-audit conduct (s.222–223 TAA); interest at the prescribed rate; criminal conviction — fine up to ZAR 50,000 and/or imprisonment up to 2 years per offence (s.235 TAA), plus fraud prosecution at common law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false ITR14 declarations can be convicted in their personal capacity; SARS may pursue civil restitution and, under s.162 TAA, obtain a warrant of arrest or departure-ban order where there is evidence the director will leave South Africa to evade payment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the (Pty) Ltd as a factoring or invoicing shell for a foreign related party, with no South African employees, board meetings, or decision-making, and passing profits out as deductible management fees while claiming DTA dividend relief.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS reconstruction under s.103 (GAAR): disallowance of fee deductions, recharacterization of payments as deemed dividends, 75%–200% understatement penalties, denial of treaty benefits and foreign tax credits; controlled foreign company attribution under s.9D may apply in reverse flows.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts will pierce the corporate veil where the company is a facade; directors face civil restitution for misapplied funds and, in criminal cases, travel bans, disqualification, and imprisonment for fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / FICA and Beneficial Ownership Non-Compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain a CIPC beneficial-ownership register, failure to conduct customer due diligence on the offshore contract principal, or processing large Progress_ACH/wire transfers without an accounting trail or source-of-funds verification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: FICA sanctions: fines up to ZAR 10 million and/or imprisonment up to 5 years per offence for accountable institutions; money-laundering convictions attract imprisonment up to 15 years; CIPC non-compliance with beneficial-ownership obligations attracts fines up to ZAR 500,000 plus daily default penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the Public Officer can be prosecuted individually; SARS reports suspicious transactions to the Financial Intelligence Centre, and directors involved in laundering contract proceeds face criminal asset forfeiture and custodial sentences.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Non-Payment of Withheld Taxes / Reckless Trading
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deducting PAYE and DWT from employees and non-resident shareholders but not remitting them to SARS, continuing to trade while insolvent, or using client retention funds for intercompany loans.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Directors' personal liability for un-remitted PAYE, SDL and UIF under s.234 TAA; 10% late-payment penalty and prescribed-rate interest on all un-remitted amounts; delinquency declaration under the Companies Act 2008 bars directors from holding office for 7 years or more.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: S.234 makes directors jointly and severally liable without a court order; SARS can sue the director's personal assets, obtain an attachment order, and apply for a departure-restriction order to prevent the director from leaving South Africa while tax debts persist.
